gaps.explanation: Detail = budgetary comparison schedules (budgetary basis): General p9 total resources 13,578,806, Street p10 5,283,989, Sales Tax p11 10,338,303, plus the nonmajor combining fund columns pp12-13 4,859,752 = 34,060,850. Statement p4 (GAAP): General 12,757,104, Street 5,222,882, Sales Tax 10,360,428, Nonmajor 4,859,752, Total 33,200,166. Per fund: General 12,757,104 - 13,578,806 = -821,702 (intergovernmental 1,013,179 vs 1,396,767, charges for services 3,459,130 vs 4,066,580, property 5,889,404 vs 5,833,218; the budget schedule has no sales-proceeds line, GAAP 95,839); Street 5,222,882 - 5,283,989 = -61,107 (other income 1,557 vs 372,890, intergovernmental 4,124,790 vs 4,223,315, donations 371,333 not on budget); Sales Tax 10,360,428 - 10,338,303 = 22,125 (sales tax 9,900,039 vs 9,835,833; budget adds loan repayment proceeds 15,315). -821,702 - 61,107 + 22,125 = -860,684 = gap. Printed budgetary vs GAAP basis; nonmajor detail ties exactly; no duplicate lines.

Detail: General p9 20,453,849 + Street p10 5,418,051 + Sales Tax p11 944,782 + nonmajor pp12-13 4,570,645 = 31,387,327. Statement p4 (GAAP): General 20,452,875, Street 6,751,327, Sales Tax 902,271, Nonmajor 4,570,645, Total 32,677,118. Street: GAAP prints Public works 5,606,852 + Principal payments on debt 1,020,000 + Interest 124,475 = 6,751,327, while the budgetary schedule prints only Public works 5,418,051 (no debt service rows): 6,751,327 - 5,418,051 = 1,333,276. General: 20,452,875 - 20,453,849 = -974 (GAAP shows principal 235,877 and interest 14,171 separately; budget folds them into the functions, e.g. public safety 10,185,614 vs 9,935,087). Sales Tax: 902,271 - 944,782 = -42,511 (general government 886,897 vs 938,888; public safety 15,374 vs 5,894). 1,333,276 - 974 - 42,511 = 1,289,791 = gap. Printed budgetary vs GAAP basis (debt service shown differently), not missing schedule lines.
